title: Node attribute catalog and regional routing notes
content:
Purpose and scope

This is a working notes doc capturing a proposed lightweight canonical node attribute catalog, health-signal taxonomy, and how service discovery will expose that inventory to the control plane for routing decisions across regions. Target audience: infra/platform engineers, serving-runtime owners, and SREs who will integrate routing policies with the cluster inventory API.

Non-goal: This is NOT a full rollout plan. It sketches key schemas, edge cases, and a minimal set of signals to start with.

Problems we're solving
- Routing needs consistent, machine-readable node attributes (GPU family, memory, PCI topology) to select compatible model variants and to choose cost/latency tradeoffs.
- Multi-region policies require topology awareness (AZ/region affinity), and graceful fallbacks when local capacity is constrained.
- Health signals for nodes must be standardized so the control plane can avoid degraded hardware (thermal throttling, ECC errors) and react quickly to noisy neighbors.
- Inventory must be light enough to be queried frequently by the routing layer without introducing high overhead.

High-level design principles
- Keep the attribute schema flat and stable. Consumers should be able to filter by label equality and numeric ranges. Avoid nested documents for low-latency queries.
- Distinguish static attributes (hardware labels) from dynamic telemetry (health metrics). Static attributes change on node reprovision; telemetry updates frequently and should be sharded.
- Use coarse-grained health states (OK | DEGRADED | UNAVAILABLE) derived from telemetry with transparent thresholds. Control plane only interprets the coarse state.
- Prefer eventual consistency for inventory caches; routing decisions should be conservative for cross-region fallback to avoid split-brain.

Suggested node attribute catalog (canonical labels)
- node.id = internal unique node id (string)
- node.region = e.g., us-west1, eu-central (string)
- node.az = e.g., us-west1-a (string)
- node.pool = logical pool name (string)
- cpu.cores = integer core count advertised by node (stringified int)
- mem.total_gb = integer (stringified int)
- gpu.count = integer
- gpu.family = nvidia-a100 | nvidia-h100 | amd-mi250 | t4 (controlled vocabulary)
- gpu.memory_gb = integer
- gpu.arch = ampere | hopper | cdna2 | turing
- gpu.interconnect = nvlink | pcielanes | none
- nvlink.width = numeric (if present) - used for model sharding decisions
- gpu.driver = driver version string (e.g., 525.85)
- gpu.mig.slice = boolean or string for MIG-enabled (for per-slice routing)
- node.tier = dedicated | burst | preemptible
- labels = free-form short tags (comma-separated) for operational grouping (e.g., "cost-optimized, spot, high-memory")

Rationale: Keep GPU detail minimal but sufficient for compatibility checks (family + memory + interconnect). Avoid shipping full topology maps in the canonical catalog; that can live in a separate topology service if needed.

Telemetry / health signals (dynamic, time-series)
We bucket telemetry into four categories: GPU health, device metrics, host-level, and reliability signals. Each signal gets a numeric value and a short status.
- gpu.utilization_pct (rolling 30s and 5m) -> used to detect noisy neighbors
- gpu.mem.used_gb (and percent)
- gpu.temp_celsius
- gpu.power_watts
- gpu.ecc.errors.count (incrementing counter)
- nvlink.error.rate (per-vendor counters)
- host.load1m, load5m
- host.mem.available_gb
- disk.iowait_pct
- heartbeat.last_seen_ts (timestamp)
- driver.errors.last_5m (count)

Derived health states (control-plane friendly)
- OK -> all critical signals within threshold
- DEGRADED -> one or more mid-severity signals (e.g., temp above warning threshold, sustained high utilization > 90% for 2m)
- UNAVAILABLE -> node is offline, heartbeat expired, or critical ECC/failure detected

Threshold suggestions (initial)
- heartbeat expiry: 20s
- GPU temp warning: > 85C for >120s -> DEGRADED; >95C -> UNAVAILABLE
- GPU utilization sustained > 95% for > 2 minutes -> DEGRADED (prefer routing to lower-util pools if latency-critical)
- ECC errors > 100/hour -> UNAVAILABLE (requires human review)

Inventory API and data flow (high level)
1) Node agent publishes static labels at boot and registers to the inventory service with node.id, region, az.
2) Telemetry agent streams time-series (push over gRPC or OTLP) to a telemetry ingestion tier (Prometheus/Tempo or vector->Influx) that maintains short-window aggregates and triggers derived-state evaluation.
3) Inventory service exposes two endpoints: /v1/nodes?filter=... (returns static attributes and last-known derived state) and /v1/nodes/{id}/metrics (returns recent telemetry snapshots). The first endpoint is intended for fast routing decisions.
4) Control plane caches /v1/nodes responses by region with TTL 8s and subscribes to subscription channels (pub/sub) for node state changes to invalidate caches quickly.

Query patterns for routing layer
- Find local nodes with gpu.family==nvidia-a100 AND gpu.memory_gb>=40 AND state==OK order by gpu.utilization_pct asc then by latency_estimate
- If no local candidates, expand to region, then to multi-region with cost weighting
- For canary/rollouts: prefer nodes with label rollout.canary=true and state==OK

Routing policy primitives (to be implemented in control plane)
- Compatibility filter: match required labels and ranges
- Affinity/anti-affinity: prefer same-region/az; optionally prefer pinned pools
- Cost-latency tradeoff scoring: score = alpha*estimated_latency_ms + beta*unit_cost_cents; default prefers latency for p99-sensitive routes
- Capacity backoff: if selected node(s) have sustained high utilization (> 80%) increase cost penalty dynamically to reduce allocation
- Graceful fallback: when no compatible nodes in region, progressively relax constraints (memory_gb-10%, allow gpu.family fallback to next-compatible family)

Multi-region specifics and cross-region fallback rules
- By default, prefer same-region nodes for data locality and egress cost; configured per-customer policy may force region-only routing.
- Fallback window: try local -> region -> peer-region (with cost amplification factor egress+latency multiplier). Peers are ordered by configured proximity matrix.
- A/B rollout: use region-level rollout flags; control plane can pin a percentage of requests to target region/pool using deterministic hashing on request id.

Operational concerns and edge cases
- Stale telemetry: if heartbeat expired, mark UNAVAILABLE immediately. Do not attempt to route until agent reports back.
- Partial GPU failure (ECC errors): mark node DEGRADED and avoid scheduling long generations or large-batch workloads.
- Node reprovisioning: when node reboots, static labels may change; require a full re-registration before returning to OK. Avoid auto-accepting cluster labels from untrusted images.
- Preemptible/spot pools: expose node.tier=preemptible and add extra routing penalty. For best-effort workloads only.
- MIG slices: treat each slice as a separate logical node with gpu.mig.slice labels and adjusted memory_gb value. Ensure accounting maps slice-id <-> physical device.

Instrumentation and dashboards (short list)
- Inventory health dashboard: nodes by region/az, OK/DEGRADED/UNAVAILABLE counts, trend lines
- GPU health heatmap: temp, utilization, ECC errors per family
- Routing decisions logs: sample of routing evals (filters applied, candidate counts, final scored node) — necessary for debugging fallback behavior
- Alerting: node UNAVAILABLE > 3 nodes in a pool => pager; ECC errors spike => pager to SREs; regional capacity below 10% => ops-runbook alert

Open questions / TODOs
- Finalize canonical vocabulary for gpu.family (nvidia-a100 vs a100-sxm vs a100-pcie). How granular do we make it?
- Need a compact encoding for nvlink topology for model sharding; decide whether to keep in a separate topology service.
- Eviction policy integration: how aggressively should the routing layer avoid nodes with high host.load1m vs relying on runtime to shed batches?
- Cost model inputs: how to represent spot pricing in node attributes so routing can use real-time price signals?

Immediate next steps
- Decide label vocabulary in a 1-hour sync (Asha, Jon, Elena) by 2026-03-01.
- Prototype /v1/nodes endpoint returning the static attributes + derived state; sample dataset from staging cluster. Owner: Marcus. Target: 2026-03-15
- Add simple routing filter into the control plane that honors gpu.family & state==OK (canary rollout to serving-runtime dev cluster). Owner: Jon. Target: 2026-03-22

Notes to self
- Keep the inventory schema forgiving: new labels can be added; consumers should ignore unknown labels.
- Document the derived-state calculation in Confluence (link CON-1242) so SREs can tune thresholds per region.

References
- jira: JIRA-PLAT-678 (cluster inventory RFC)
- github: github.com/redwood-inference/cluster-inventory/pull/92 (initial API)
- confluence: CON-1242 (canonical labels spec)
summary: Working notes proposing a flat node attribute catalog, health signal taxonomy, inventory API patterns, routing primitives for multi-region fallback, and operational runbooks. Contains thresholds, query examples, and action items.
